reason: E3 directly supports all key premises by reporting that nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn at GBs reduces cohesion and causes ductility loss, and that shifting segregation to secondary phases avoids this. E1 and E2 are not needed for these premises; E1 speculates about nanoscale precipitates in a different alloy, and E2 describes ductile fracture in a multi-phase wire, neither of which directly supports the specific mechanism proposed.
premises: Nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn at grain boundaries occurs in single-phase CrMnFeCoNi HEA
Such nanoclustering reduces grain boundary cohesion
Reduced GB cohesion promotes intergranular cracking and ductility loss
Shifting segregation into preexisting Cr-rich secondary phases avoids ductility loss
